HUMAN RIGHTS · INTERNATIONAL JUSTICE

NaviPillay.

A South African jurist whose career connected anti-apartheid legal practice, international criminal courts and United Nations human-rights leadership.

Start the study lensPeace overview
ROLEJurist and human-rights leader
INSTITUTIONSSouth African High Court · ICTR · ICC · UN
CORE PRINCIPLEPeace depends on law applying to everyone

WHY SHE MATTERS

Build peace through accountability

Pillay’s career shows international law as practical infrastructure. Courts and human-rights institutions preserve testimony, define crimes, protect rights and challenge impunity—even when enforcement is slow or politically contested.

Accountability and rights protection

Judgments and public findings strengthen the conditions for durable peace.

THREE-PASS REVIEW

Read the contribution from three angles

ACTIVE LENS

The person

Pillay began legal practice under apartheid, defended its opponents and became the first non-white woman judge on South Africa’s High Court before serving in major international judicial and human-rights roles.
